domain: Technology Law / Software Liability / Consumer Protection
topic_summary: Analysis of the legal designation 'beta' as applied to software, examining the structural contest between industry's expansive reading (blanket liability shield) and regulatory/consumer-protection reading (temporary warning label with bounded scope). The kernel is a shared commitment to the 'beta' designation's legal significance; the readings instantiate different constraint structures over who bears risk of software defects.

key_entities: Software developers/publishers (industry actors asserting 'beta' as liability shield)
Regulatory bodies (FTC, EU consumer protection agencies interpreting 'beta' scope)
End users/consumers (bearing risk under expansive 'beta' reading)
Legal doctrine of 'beta' designation (the contested kernel: industry practice codified as norm)
Product liability frameworks (traditional consumer protection regimes that 'beta' potentially bypasses)
key_tensions: Industry liability minimization vs consumer risk allocation (developers vs users on defect responsibility)
Innovation velocity vs consumer protection (permissive beta deployment vs safety gatekeeping)
key_mechanisms: Beta designation as EULA/ToS clause (contractual mechanism purporting to disclaim liability)
Regulatory enforcement discretion (agencies' willingness to challenge overbroad 'beta' claims)
Market signaling ambiguity (consumers uncertain whether 'beta' means 'experimental' or 'nearly final')
key_absences: Temporal boundary enforcement: no institutional mechanism tracks when 'permanent beta' becomes abuse
Severity-based liability carveouts: whether critical systems (medical, financial) can invoke 'beta' shield at all

axes.human_readable: Expansive Shield Reading (Beta as Blanket Liability Waiver)
axes.structural_delta: Beta designation interpreted as comprehensive waiver of developer liability for all defects, indefinite duration
axes.primary_observable: EULA language scope; judicial enforcement of beta-based liability disclaimers; duration of 'beta' designation in production software
axes.selection_reason: Reading 1 of contested kernel: instantiates high-extraction constraint (users bear all risk)

axes.human_readable: Narrow Warning Reading (Beta as Temporary Consumer Disclosure)
axes.structural_delta: Beta designation interpreted as time-bounded warning requiring genuine testing phase, preserving base liability
axes.primary_observable: Regulatory guidance on beta duration limits; judicial rejection of perpetual beta status; consumer protection enforcement actions
axes.selection_reason: Reading 2 of contested kernel: instantiates coordination constraint (temporary testing regime)

axes.human_readable: Severity Carve-Out Reading (Beta Inapplicable to Critical Systems)
axes.structural_delta: Beta designation categorically unavailable for life-safety/financial systems regardless of testing status
axes.primary_observable: Sector-specific regulations (FDA medical device beta rules, financial services software deployment requirements); judicial categorical prohibitions
axes.selection_reason: Reading 3 of contested kernel: instantiates domain-specific physical constraint (safety requirements override beta designation)

axes.structural_delta: Consumers systematically misinterpret beta signals due to industry 'permanent beta' normalization
axes.primary_observable: Consumer survey data on beta risk perception; market adoption rates of beta-labeled vs GA-labeled products
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: market coordination failure feeding expansive reading, but structurally redundant with consumer victimization already captured in reading 1

axes.human_readable: Temporal Boundary Enforcement Absence (No Beta Duration Limits)
axes.structural_delta: Legal frameworks lack institutional mechanism to challenge indefinite beta designation
axes.primary_observable: Absence of statutory beta duration caps; regulatory enforcement action frequency against perpetual beta
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: structural absence enabling expansive reading, but captured implicitly in reading 1 vs reading 2 contrast (indefinite vs time-bounded)

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Consumer misinterpretation of beta signals due to permanent beta normalization
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Consumer victimization already captured in expansive_shield_reading; signaling failure is mechanism of extraction not independent constraint

deferred_axes.structural_delta: No institutional mechanism to challenge indefinite beta designation
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Structural absence enabling expansive reading, but contrast between indefinite and time-bounded beta already captured in reading 1 vs reading 2

omegas.description: EU GDPR Article 25 and Product Liability Directive may categorically reject beta shields for data processing/physical products, creating jurisdictional arbitrage opportunities. If expansive reading only viable in US, does that reclassify it from Snare to Piton (atrophied sovereignty)?
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) + absence of international harmonization in extraction

omegas.description: Emerging AI liability frameworks (EU AI Act, algorithmic accountability bills) may bypass beta designation entirely by imposing strict liability for high-risk systems. Does severity_carve_out_reading become dominant framework, making readings 1 and 2 legacy doctrine for low-risk software only?
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) + domain evolution trajectory

omegas.description: Does open source software under permissive licenses (MIT, Apache) constitute a fourth reading where beta designation is genuine mutual waiver rather than extractive Snare? No commercial beneficiary changes constraint type.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 1 (Operational Medium) + beneficiary structure variance

omegas.description: What defines 'critical system' for severity_carve_out_reading? Financial apps handling $10 vs $10M? Medical decision support vs diagnostic? Boundary ambiguity may allow migration from reading 3 to reading 1 via definitional capture.
omegas.source: Classification instability in reading 3 mountain hypothesis

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel decomposition valid: three readings instantiate genuinely different constraints (high extraction Snare vs low-coordination Scaffold vs domain-specific Mountain). Readings share substrate (beta designation) but emit different beneficiary/victim structures and epsilon values. Axiom contradictions documented in commitment_system_recognition.

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The legal/industry designation 'beta' for software, codified as a norm granting special status claims regarding liability allocation
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Interpretive legitimacy contested: industry asserts self-regulatory authority via standard contracts; regulators/courts assert state authority via consumer protection frameworks

readings.commitment: Beta designation constitutes comprehensive liability waiver; indefinite duration permissible; applies to all software contexts
readings.authority_grounding: Industry self-regulation via standard EULA practices; contract law freedom-of-contract principle
readings.expected_structural_delta: High extraction: developers externalize all defect costs to users; users enter victim set; no temporal or severity boundaries

readings.commitment: Beta designation is time-bounded testing disclosure; base product liability preserved; duration must be genuine testing phase
readings.authority_grounding: Regulatory consumer protection mandates; judicial scrutiny of unconscionable contract terms
readings.expected_structural_delta: Low coordination: temporary testing regime requiring good-faith bounds; liability shield expires with testing phase; users informed but not victimized

readings.commitment: Beta designation categorically unavailable for life-safety, financial, or other critical systems regardless of testing status or disclosure
readings.authority_grounding: Sector-specific safety regulations (FDA, financial services prudential rules); strict liability doctrines
readings.expected_structural_delta: Domain-specific physical constraint: safety requirements and harm severity override contractual liability allocation; beta unavailable as mechanism in high-stakes domains

axiom_contradictions.basis: Expansive reading holds contractual freedom permits indefinite liability waiver; narrow reading holds consumer protection law sets mandatory liability floors. No framework holds both: either contract trumps consumer protection or consumer protection limits contract.

Expansive reading holds beta applies universally to all software contexts; severity carve-out holds safety-critical domains categorically prohibit beta liability shields. No framework holds both: either beta universality or domain-specific categorical prohibition.

These readings can coexist: narrow warning allows temporary beta with preserved liability for non-critical systems; severity carve-out prohibits beta entirely for critical systems. Not axiom-contradictory; complementary scope-based rules.
